sources.claim: George Town is recognised by UNESCO as an exceptional multicultural trading town from 500 years of East-West exchange in the Straits of Malacca.
Melaka and George Town were inscribed on the World Heritage List on 7 July 2008 under criteria (ii), (iii) and (iv).
The protected George Town heritage area is divided into a core zone and a buffer zone with close to 100 heritage sites.
In 2012 George Town commissioned Ernest Zacharevic; his Children on a Bicycle mural became Penang's tourism icon.
In November 2024 Ernest Zacharevic restored four of his original iconic murals after 12 years.
Penang street art is best explored self-guided with a walking trail and map covering the mural clusters.
The Marking George Town project placed 52 wrought-iron caricature sculptures by Sculpture at Work to explain street histories.
The steel rod caricatures are a comic-art trail telling George Town's history.
Leong San Tong Khoo Kongsi is an ornate Chinese clan house in George Town.
Khoo Kongsi is open 9:00-17:00 daily; entry is RM15 for adult foreigners and RM1 for children.
Kek Lok Si grounds are free (8:30-17:30); the inclined lift and the Pagoda of Ten Thousand Buddhas (~RM2) carry small fees.
Kek Lok Si is topped by a 30.2 m bronze Kuan Yin statue completed in 2002.
The Penang Hill funicular runs 6:30am-11pm; foreigner adult return is RM40, Fast Lane RM80.
The Habitat on Penang Hill offers the Langur Way canopy walk and Curtis Crest tree-top walk.
The Habitat tickets start around RM52 with 10% off for booking 7+ days ahead; Curtis Crest closes for maintenance from 13 May 2026.
The Pinang Peranakan Mansion is a restored Straits-Chinese mansion museum.
The Peranakan Mansion is open 9:30-17:00 with admission around RM20-25.
Fort Cornwallis, built 1786, is the oldest British structure in Malaysia; entry RM20 for adults.
Fort Cornwallis entry is payable by card only, not cash.
The clan jetties are free stilt-house water villages; Chew Jetty is the largest and most visited.
Chew Jetty is a living residential community; visitors are asked to come roughly 9am-9pm.
Wat Chaiyamangalaram houses a 33 m reclining Buddha and faces the Burmese temple across the road.
Dhammikarama, built 1803, is the only Burmese Buddhist temple in Malaysia and is free to enter.
Kapitan Keling Mosque is free to non-Muslim visitors outside prayer times, with robes lent at the door.
Kuan Yin Teng is Penang's oldest Chinese temple, dating to 1728, dedicated to Guan Yin.
The Goddess of Mercy (Kuan Yin) Temple is a listed George Town cultural-heritage site.
Penang National Park is open daily; foreigner entry is RM50 (card only) and boats can be arranged on the day.
The hike to Turtle Beach (Pantai Kerachut) is about 3.8 km linear, roughly 1.5 hours.
Turtle Beach has a turtle conservation centre; nesting season runs September to December.
Monkey Beach is reachable by a forest trail in Penang National Park.
The Blue Mansion runs 45-min guided tours at 11am and 3:30pm for RM25 (max 24 people), and the courtyard featured in Crazy Rich Asians.
Penang's rainy season brings mostly short downpours rather than all-day rain; festivals affect timing too.
Penang's dry season runs December to March with highs around 31 C.
Mid-November to mid-February is the best weather window but is peak season, so book ahead.
The Snake Temple in Bayan Lepas is free (6:00-19:00), once home to pit vipers, with a snake farm (RM5) attached.
Hean Boo Thean is a free floating Kuan Yin temple off Weld Quay near the clan jetties.
Sri Mahamariamman is Penang's oldest Hindu temple, with free admission, in Little India.
George Town's City Hall is a Victorian building constructed in 1903 and opened in 1906.
The Town Hall, completed in the 1880s, is George Town's oldest municipal building.
Batu Ferringhi is Penang's main resort beach strip with watersports and seafood.
Batu Ferringhi Beach is a free, popular swimmable beach about 15 minutes from George Town.
The George Town heritage core is compact and best explored on foot in comfortable shoes.
Khoo Kongsi is widely rated as the grandest clan house in George Town.
Fast Lane funicular tickets are recommended at peak times to skip the queues.
The Dhammikarama Burmese Temple is open 9am-5pm with free entry.
